scoring_rationale: Class semantics and conclusion binding measure sound (C1/C2/C3/C7/C9 pass; the contested critical defect HF-06 is refuted). Three independently reproduced blocking defects are provenance/completeness, not physics: an unresolved class-contract pointer against the authoritative canonical F0 tree, a parser-dependent future-dated effective revision timestamp, and an undefined normative symbol in conclusion.statement_formal. Hence revise (3.0), not reject; the class content would be acceptable once these three are fixed and republished.

hard_failures.name: undefined_normative_symbol_in_statement_formal

measured.line: conclusion.statement_formal line 251: 'AF_{I+}(M_D) and complete(I+_D) and not exists visible_singularity_from_I_plus(M_D)'

hard_failures.why_blocking: The schema declares itself bound to statement_formal (line 255), but that formal statement uses a predicate defined nowhere in the document or in either F0 tree; complete(I+_D) is likewise prose-only. The intended meaning is recoverable from quantifiers.formal, but the normative conclusion is not self-contained, so its equivalence to the canonical F0 conclusion text is a reader reconstruction. Independently measured by worker-090 HF090-03 and flash-19's second HF-06.
hard_failures.repair: define AF_{I+}(M_D) and complete(I+_D) in a definitions block (or inline them in statement_formal), and record the F0-conclusion equivalence as a checkable identity.

findings.text: HF-06 (deepseek-flash-19, severity critical) is REFUTED. It claims quantifiers.formal (whole-curve single-q, lines 54-55 with D5) is strictly weaker than visibility.definition (tail single-q, line 220). For the class's own D4 objects (future-directed causal geodesics) and the causal past J^-(q), the two predicates are equivalent: if a tail gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) then for every t<t0 causality gives gamma(t) <= gamma(t0) <= q, so gamma is contained in J^-(q); the converse is immediate. Machine evidence: exhaustive enumeration of all 241 strict partial orders on 2-4 elements, every chain and every q, finds 0 whole-vs-tail divergences (C7); the same harness finds 26 divergences when past-closure is dropped (teeth control), and 0 over past-closed sets. quantifiers.formal and quantifiers.negation therefore remain exact negations, and no datum is classified differently by the two phrasings.

The five visibility sites are textually split: quantifiers.formal, domains.D5 and visibility.witness_protocol use whole-curve single-q; visibility.definition, quantifiers.negation, conclusion.statement_formal and the canonical F0 conclusion use the tail predicate. The line-220 rationale ('requiring the whole geodesic ... would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region') is mathematically incorrect, but semantically inert by F-040-01. Recommended one-line fix: unify on the tail predicate and state the past-closure lemma; this also removes the divergence the canonical F0 revision flags as 'review HF-06'.

The single recorded accept at this hash (reviews/F1-review-lead-audit-r2.json, 4.5) records no disposition of HF090-01/HF090-02/HF090-03, which I reproduce. That accept cannot be counted as covering these three majors; the gate coverage scan should treat this target as still needing two accepts after the majors are fixed.

Publication pair F0 is still divergent (canonical 276009f4 vs authoring c8e979a1) as of the review window; F1/F2a/F2b pairs are aligned and FROZEN revision 26 lists the same sha256 for schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml. The F0 divergence does not bind this F1 verdict but remains a G-F0 blocker.
